text: A multinomial logistic classifier maps zt to failure classes C0–C3:

with 6 × 4 = 24 parameters trained on 900 trajectories (<0.1 ms inference). Actions: C0 passes; C1 regenerates with constrained decoding; C2 soft-invalidates stale chunks; C3 re-scopes the retrieval namespace.

text: Standard single-turn retrieval benchmarks evaluate isolated, single-session lookups, lacking the multi-session temporal dependencies of long-horizon deployments. LONGAGENT-RECONBENCH fills this gap: 1,200 trajectories (300 per domain: MED clinical, MUN zoning, FIN regulatory, SWE repository maintenance), 81,370 chunks, 30.2 turns/trajectory on average. Contamination affects 29.8–36.5% of turns; hallu- cination, 19.5–26.1%.

text: Annotation & Dataset Split. Ground truth was produced by 12 certified domain specialists (three per domain), each label- ing every turn with its true epistemic state (C0–C3). Double-blind cross-annotation on 20% of turns yielded strong inter-annotator agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.84; Fleiss’ κ = 0.82). The official split comprises 900 training, 100 validation, and 200 held-out test trajectories.

text: Construction & Leakage Control. Each trajectory is gen- erated in three phases: (i) backbone execution—GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet agents operate a FAISS-backed episodic store (BGE-M3 embeddings, 256-token chunks, k=5) across 5–15 sessions, committing reflections unconstrained so C1 failures emerge naturally; (ii) controlled perturbation—at mile- stones tupdate ∈ [0.3T, 0.7T], explicit world-state updates inject C2 material while unrelated sessions are interleaved for C3 collisions; (iii) verification—three specialists per domain label every turn against the authoritative update log, so each failure instance carries an auditable provenance record shipped with the benchmark. All splits are trajectory-disjoint and template-disjoint: query templates, update patterns, and named entities are partitioned into per-split pools with no overlap. Residual risk—stylistic overlap of the two backbones—is discussed in Section V.

text: Implementation Details. Dense embeddings E(·) use BGE-M3 [25] (d = 1024); natural language inference (NLI) scores use DeBERTa-v3-large [26]. Atomic claims are extracted as the top-3 dependency-parse propositions per response. Hyper- parameters α=0.65 and β=3.2 were selected on the validation split (stable within ±0.10: ∆AUROC<0.005).

text: Baselines. BM25 [23], Contriever [24], BGE-M3 [25], Cross-Encoder NLI [26], FACTSCORE [13], SELFCHECKGPT [12], GRAPH-RAG [21]; single-turn baselines receive the top-k chunks as grounding for fairness.

text: Metrics & Hardware. We report binary F1 and AUROC for detection (threshold from validation), macro F1 for 4-class attribution, and AUPRC; significance uses paired bootstrap over 1,000 trajectory-clustered resamples (p < 0.001), stable across 5 seeds (±0.4% F1). Longitudinal runs use 40 held-out trajectories (10 per domain, 100 turns). Profiling: NVIDIA RTX 4090 / AMD EPYC 7763.

text: Table I shows that on contamination detection, RECON- TRACE achieves AUROC 0.942 (binary F1 90.0%)—+10.4 and +13.8 percentage points over SELFCHECKGPT and GRAPH-RAG—and on hallucination detection AUROC 0.938 (F1 88.6%), exceeding second-best SELFCHECKGPT (0.865). Dense retrievers score lower because they match similarity without checking temporal or logical coherence. Fig. 2(a) shows the empirical SRCA densities: clean turns cluster at µ=0.85, contaminated at 0.42, hallucinatory at 0.18; the threshold θ∗=0.62 separates clean from failure turns, and resid- ual C1/C2/3 overlap is resolved by the attribution classifier
